title: Andromeda
subtitle: Will it crash into us?
yt_title: Will Andromeda Crash Into Us? 🌌 | Ep. 19 #shorts
description:
Episode 19 of a daily journey through the universe. 🌌
We visit the Andromeda galaxy: 2.5 million light-years away, visible with your own eyes, racing toward us at 100 km/s, and why a 2025 study says a crash is now only a 50/50 chance.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 20: Next stop, dark matter. The invisible stuff holding galaxies together.

segments.text: Andromeda is the biggest galaxy near us, about two and a half million light-years away.
segments.headline: 2.5 million light-years away

segments.text: On a dark night, you can see it without a telescope. It's the farthest thing most people can see with their own eyes.
segments.headline: Visible with your eyes

segments.text: It's racing toward us at about a hundred kilometers per second.
For years, scientists said the two galaxies would crash in about four and a half billion years.
segments.headline: A crash in 4.5 billion years?

segments.text: But in twenty twenty-five, new data from Hubble and Gaia changed the story. Now it's only about a fifty-fifty chance in the next ten billion years.

visual.label: chance of a crash
visual.sub: In the next 10 billion years (2025 study)

segments.text: And even if they collide, stars are so far apart that almost none would hit each other.
segments.headline: Stars would almost never touch

segments.text: Tomorrow, we discover the invisible stuff holding galaxies together. Next stop: dark matter. Follow, so you don't miss episode twenty.
